text:
marta: Hey — found a suspicious object in partner-logs S3 bucket that looks like a wrapped KMS blob containing Vault transit ciphertext. Not sure if partner accidentally uploaded a backup with wrapped secrets. Path: s3://partner-logs/ingest/2026-03-20/backup-20260320.blob

ben: Can you paste the object key + size and a sha256?

marta: backup-20260320.blob (4.1 MB) sha256: 9f2c4e1a... (pasting truncated)

marta: Quick check: the blob header matches our KMS-wrap format (starts with "KMSv1"). Might be transit-wrapped, not raw vault kv.

samir: @marta good catch. Immediate steps: 1) remove partner ingest SA from KMS decrypt grants 2) snapshot and isolate object for forensics 3) create incident ticket. Can infra run a revoke on the key binding?

infra-oncall: On it. Will remove the IAM binding and snapshot the object. Running: `gcloud kms keys remove-iam-policy-binding projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/partner/cryptoKeys/ingest-key --member=serviceAccount:partner-ingest@partner.iam.gserviceaccount.com --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter`

infra-oncall: done. IAM binding removed. Took a copy of the blob to gs://redwood-forensics/7889990000/backup-20260320.blob

security-bot: Incident INC-2026-045 created (priority: P2) — assigned to eng-security.

jess: We should assume the worst: partner blob may allow rewrap/unseal of Vault data if transit key was used. Plan: rotate Vault transit key, rewrap affected ciphertexts with new key, revoke old key. Samir, can you coordinate with Vault ops?

samir: Yes. Steps I propose:
- create new transit key in Vault (transit/new-ingest-2026-03-20)
- use vault rewrap API to rewrap ciphertexts we control 
- for partner data (we don't have plaintext), ask partner to rewrap or we provide a debug flow if contract permits

marta: Partner timeline: they said it was a mistaken backup upload, they will cooperate, but they also confirm the SA was used for ingestion earlier this month.

ben: We need to scope blast radius. Which systems use that KMS key? Any long-lived tokens or service accounts with decrypt perms?

infra-oncall: Quick audit: key was granted to partner-ingest SA and our backup-archiver SA. Only those two current bindings (after removal). No human-granted IAM. No compute instances with attached key.

samir: For Vault: I'm creating new transit key now and enabling key derivation/signer options off. Running: `vault write -f transit/keys/new-ingest-2026-03-20`

samir: Next I'll trigger a rewrap for any ciphertexts in vault mount `secret/ingest/*` that were wrapped by the old transit key. Running a dry-run first to list affected keys.

jess: Good. Also we should rotate GCP KMS key (create a new cryptoKey version and disable old versions) once Vault rewrap is complete. Also rotate any long-lived tokens that partner-ingest SA might have touched (if any).

marta: Forensics note: I've extracted a small sample header and sent to @legal for TLP guidance. We might need a narrow disclosure.

infra-oncall: Rewrap dry-run results: 27 ciphertexts referenced the old transit key under secret/ingest. Will attempt automated rewrap in a maintenance window (30m).

ben: Coordinate with product owners for secret consumers — we should avoid breaking live jobs. Schedule a canary rewrap on 1 consumer first.

samir: Canary rewrap succeeded against ingest-worker config (no downtime). Proceeding with bulk rewrap now. Command: `vault write transit/rewrap ciphertext=@cipherlist.json to_key=new-ingest-2026-03-20`

infra-oncall: Bulk rewrap finished. All 27 items rewrapped. Backups for old ciphertexts saved to gs://redwood-forensics/7889990000/old-ciphertexts/

jess: Nice. Next: create a new KMS key version and update Vault plugin (if it uses cloud kms seal) to point to new key. Also rotate any archived backups that used KMS wrap.

marta: Partner confirms they rotated their ingestion tokens and deleted the accidental backup from their S3. They provided a signed attestation.

ben: Action items summary:
- infra: removed IAM binding (done)
- samir: created new transit key + rewrapped vault ciphertexts (done)
- jess: will rotate KMS versions + update configs (in progress)
- marta: coordinate partner attestation + legal (in progress)

jess: KMS new version created: projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/partner/cryptoKeys/ingest-key/cryptoKeyVersions/3. Disabled old version 2. Updating cloud-kms-seal config and rolling deploy to Vault nodes.

infra-oncall: Deploy roll started for vault-seal-updater. Rolling restart of 3 nodes, 1 at a time.

security-bot: INC-2026-045 updated: remediation mitigations applied, monitoring enabled.

marta: Marking this thread for postmortem. Please add timeline notes to INC-2026-045 and add owners for the follow-ups: RBAC hardening, periodic key binding audit, partner onboarding checklist update.

ben: Agreed. I'll own RBAC audit. Jess — can you own update to onboarding checklist?

jess: Yep. Will add a step to verify backups are never uploaded to partner buckets and require an allowed list for S3 destinations.

samir: I'll draft a small runbook for rewraps and emergency key eviction, and link to the incident.

marta: Thanks all. Closing in Slack — will keep INC open for postmortem and follow-ups. :thumbsup:
